answer: Each Ember Cartographer node issues a non‑transferable opal token tied to a cryptographic proof of hardware‑bound shale enclave, then locks any reward in a time‑vested ember contract that releases only one unit per day per identity. When a new identity appears, it must first acquire a shale enclave and purchase the opal, paying the full daily cost upfront; the contract then drips rewards at the fixed rate, so a Sybil farm must front‑load cash for every fake node. The attacker’s expense grows linearly with the number of identities, quickly outpacing any profit from the slow vesting.
